title: Quiet retreat notes: inference tradeoffs + quick experiments
content:
Context: took two days offline (no meetings) to map out recurring puzzles in long-context inference. Rough, noisy — meant for me and a couple collaborators. High-level goals: 1) collect concise takeaways from recent papers/blogs I read at the retreat, 2) sketch 2-3 tiny experiments we can run this sprint that fit into Dedicated test cluster, 3) list pragmatic heuristics for staging quant/eviction changes.

Retreat takeaways (short bullets)
- KV sharding + selective eviction seems more robust than global LRU for multi-session workloads. Paper: "Adaptive KV Shard Routing" (ArXiv 2026) — idea: split cache by topic embedding clusters, evict within cluster. Takeaway: clustering reduces catastrophic eviction for conversational tails.
- Quant-stability notes: 4-bit symmetric quant (per-channel) with small calibration set outperforms post-train static scales at long context tails; still see hallucination drift after token 8k for some demos. Important: monitor both likelihood and n-gram overlap for regressions.
- Latency-econ: batching policy that uses a short randomized delay (6–12ms) plus priority fast-path for interactive sessions gave ~12% lower cost at 99th p99 compared to pure fixed-window batching on our sample workload.
- Fallback stacks: keep a midway model (e.g., 4-bit 8B variant) as a warm fallback rather than immediately falling to CPU for graceful degradation. Hint: maintain KV compatibility metadata so fallbacks can continue conversation without re-tokenizing.

Paper sketches + 1-line actionable
- "Clustered-KV Eviction" (2026): cluster by query embedding, maintain per-cluster LRU. Action: prototype on small trace (1000 sessions) and add cluster id tag in KV store. Metric: session-level token reuse rate.
- "TinyQuant: calibration for 4-bit LM" (blog): calibration set of ~2000 tokens across domains crucial. Action: build a small calibration corpus of customer prompts + public web snippets. Automate calibration run during model onboarding.
- "Sparse Routing for Retrieval-Augmented Generation": gating at KV fetch time can reduce fetch set size by 40% w/o hurting recall. Action: try 2 gating thresholds on RAG demo for search latency reduction.

Mini experiment plan (2-week, low risk)
- Experiment A: Clustered eviction smoke
  - Data: 24h of anonymized prefix traces (already available in s3://ri-infra/tmp/kv-sample)
  - Implementation: augment kv-store mock to accept cluster_id tag (python handler ~150 LOC).
  - Evaluations: hit rate per-session, worst-case rate (bottom 5% users), generation perplexity on held-out prompts.
  - Success criteria: +8% overall hit rate, <1% delta in generation quality.

- Experiment B: Quant calibration automation
  - Data: small calibration corpora per domain (docs + code + chat).
  - Steps: run post-train calibration for candidate model TinyLlama-8B-qdq, measure answer similarity vs fp16 baseline on 200 eval prompts.
  - Metrics: semantic-similarity (bert-score), token-level divergence, hallucination triggers (simple detector).
  - Success criteria: semantic-sim >= 0.98 baseline AND 20-25% cost improvement.

- Experiment C: Fast-path batching ablation (prod-like)
  - Toy harness: run 10k synthetic interactive sessions against current batching policy vs randomized-delay policy.
  - Metric: mean latency, p95/p99, tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens.
  - Success criteria: p99 improved or cost reduced with <5% mean-latency regression.

Notes-to-self (pragmatic heuristics)
- Add KV metadata: model_version, cluster_id, creation_ts. Keep creation_ts for TTL heuristics that prefer older keys to evict last.
- For canary quant rollouts: start with low-traffic dedicated pool, run synthetic probes (diverse prompts) every 15m, auto-roll-back if any probe drops below quality thresh.
- When testing fallback models, preserve tokenization consistency: prefer fallbacks with identical tokenizer if possible to avoid alignment artifacts.

Quick commands / pseudo-ops
- Extract trace sample: aws s3 cp s3://ri-infra/tmp/kv-sample/trace-20261003.json ./ && jq 'map(select(.session_len>50))' trace-20261003.json > long-sessions.json
- Local perf harness run (docker): docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/data ri/kv-harness:canary --trace ./long-sessions.json --policy clustered-evict
- Calibration runner sketch: python calibrate_quant.py --model tiny-llama-8b --calib-corpus ./calib/* --out scales.json

Open questions / unknowns
- How sensitive are users' subjective quality metrics to small KL shifts introduced by 4-bit quant? Quant papers cite BLEU-like metrics but real convo quality might be non-linear.
- Cluster id drift: queries may hop clusters mid-session. Eviction strategy must be tolerant (hybrid global+cluster counters?). Consider soft membership.
- Cost modeling: need to incorporate tail risk (p99) into per-token unit economics; current unit-cost calc assumes mean latency.

Follow-ups (next actions)
- Draft a short PRD (1 pager) for clustered-KV experiment; share with Rina for feasibility notes by Oct 8.
- Spin up a tiny Dedicated pool (2 cards) for A/B of batching policies; ask infra to reserve by Oct 11 (JIRA-OPS-1987).
- Build a ~2k token calibration corpus: collect 500 customer anonymized prompts + 1.5k from public web. Assign to Devon.

Random musings (notes-to-self, messy)
- Could we do ephemeral sub-caches keyed on conversation topic signals (embedding centroid) and evict entire sub-cache when memory pressure high? Might reduce cross-topic interference.
- For demos, show cost delta as "$ per 1M interactive tokens at p95" instead of mean to keep SRE/product conversations honest.

End of retreat sketch — rough, will refine into a short PRD and a slide for eng sync. Keep this doc as single-source brainstorming; prune and convert to confluence PRD when ready.
